answer: At most 5 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a wharf tag. The basalt cap is upheld at intake and zenith shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, as each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 32 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
